CHIEF COMPLAINT
Kidney stone with left back pain.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient reports pain that started approximately three days ago in the left back. The pain is constant and has been traveling lower toward the groin. Patient reports inability to get comfortable. Patient began seeing blood in urine this morning. Patient denies fever but reports some chills and nausea. Patient denies being able to eat due to pain. Patient states she has had two previous kidney stone episodes, usually taking three to four days to pass. This is her third kidney stone. Patient has tried Tylenol and ibuprofen for pain management with limited relief. Patient is able to urinate.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Denies chest pain. Denies abdominal pain. Reports chills and nausea. Denies fever.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Hypertension
Diabetes mellitus
Recurrent kidney stones (third episode)
Grade 2 out of 6 systolic ejection murmur

MEDICATIONS
Norvasc 2.5 mg for hypertension
Metformin 500 mg for diabetes
Tylenol as needed
Ibuprofen as needed

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient reports enjoying French fries and has difficulty with dietary salt restriction.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital signs: Blood pressure elevated at time of visit, attributed to pain.
Heart: Grade 2 out of 6 systolic ejection murmur appreciated, known previously.
Lungs: Clear bilaterally, no crackles or wheezes.
Abdomen: Tenderness to palpation, no rebound or guarding.
Flanks: CVA tenderness on the right.

RESULTS
Pre-visit glucose testing: Patient reports fasting blood sugars in low 100s. Previous glucose test couple of months ago was around 300. A1C from last visit: 7.3.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Kidney stone, third occurrence, with associated right flank inflammation. Prescribed oxycodone 5 mg every 6 to 8 hours as needed for pain. Continue Tylenol for breakthrough pain. Patient instructed to push fluids to help pass stone. Provided urine strainer to strain urine if stone is passed. Referral placed to urology for evaluation given recurrent kidney stones, to be seen even if stone passes within next couple of days. Hypertension: Continue Norvasc 2.5 mg, blood pressures currently adequate. Patient to continue monitoring blood pressure with home cuff at least three times per week. Diabetes: Continue Metformin 500 mg. Referral placed to nutrition/dietitian for dietary counseling and salt restriction guidance, with goal of potentially discontinuing medications in the future.
